text: Hi, my name is Bread. I'm a big coffee lover, so I guess I'll start there. I can't really start my day without a cup of coffee, and this morning was no different. I had one before I came to take this test, and I'm already looking forward to another one once it's over. I work in IT at Samsung Heavy Industries. I'm in charge of our IT systems, so my days are pretty busy. I live in an apartment with my wife, and we're pretty much homebodies. In my free time, I like listening to music, playing computer games, and reading. So, yeah, that's me in a nutshell: coffee, my wife, and my computer. I'm happy to be here, and I hope I do well today!

I'm into a lot of different music, but if I had to pick, I'd say K-pop. When I'm working, though, I like to put on some jazz or lo-fi music in the background. It helps me focus, and it goes really well with a cup of coffee. As for my favorite group, it's a girl group called Rescene. I've been a fan of theirs for a while now. Their songs are catchy and full of energy, and their vocals are really strong. And here's the fun part: one of the members is from Geoje, the same city where I live! So I feel a special connection to them, and I'm kind of proud of her. Whenever I need to unwind after a long day, I put on their playlist, and it just melts the stress away.

I listen to music pretty much all the time. On my way to work, I listen in the car. At my desk, I put on headphones and play music while I work. And at home, I play music on my computer when I'm gaming or reading in my room. I mostly stream music on my phone, so I don't really listen to the radio anymore. As for concerts, I've actually never been to one. Honestly, I'd love to go, especially to a Rescene concert. I'm sure the energy is totally different from listening at home. Maybe I'll finally go next year, and I might even drag my wife along!

I got into music in middle school. I used to carry around a portable CD player, and I'd listen to the same album over and over again. Back then, I liked loud, upbeat songs, like rock and dance music. I wanted music that was fun and full of energy. These days, though, my taste has changed a bit. I still like K-pop, but I also go for calmer songs, like jazz and lo-fi, especially when I'm working. I think it's because my life is so busy now that I want something relaxing. Also, the way I listen has changed. In the past, I had to buy CDs. Now I can stream anything I want in seconds. Looking back, it's kind of funny how much things have changed.

My favorite beach is Deokpo Beach, which is right here in Geoje. Geoje is an island, so we have lots of beaches, but Deokpo is my favorite because it's close to my home. It only takes about 20 minutes by car. It's not a huge beach, but it's quiet and peaceful. The water is clear and calm, and you can see boats and islands in the distance. The sunsets are beautiful, too. There are also a few cute cafes nearby, which is a big plus for me. I go there a couple of times a month in the summer, usually with my wife. It's my go-to place when I want to clear my head. I'm lucky to live so close to the sea.

The last time I went to the beach was this past summer. My wife and I took a road trip along the west coast, and we stopped at a beach on the way. It was very different from the beaches in Geoje. It was incredibly wide and flat, and the sand was soft and warm. The water was far out, so we took off our shoes and walked along the shore. What I liked most was the sunset. We sat on the sand with iced coffee, of course, and just watched the sun go down. The whole sky turned red. I took a ton of pictures, but none of them really did it justice. It was so relaxing, and I felt like all my stress had disappeared.

One trip I'll never forget was the west coast road trip I took with my wife this summer. We wanted to get away after a really stressful month at work. Geoje is on the south coast, and the tide there doesn't change much. So when we got to the west coast, the tide was out, and the sea had gone out so far that there was a huge mudflat instead of water. I'd never seen anything like it! We decided to walk out onto the mudflat, barefoot, and we were collecting little clams and chasing crabs. We were having so much fun that we lost track of time. Suddenly, I noticed the water was coming back in, really fast. We had to run back to the shore, laughing and screaming. I tripped, fell face-first into the mud, and got covered from head to toe! My wife couldn't stop laughing. In the end, we had to wash off at a gas station. It was messy, but it was one of the funniest days of our lives. That's why it was so memorable.

We have lots of gatherings and celebrations in Korea. The biggest ones are Chuseok and Lunar New Year. On those holidays, the whole family gets together, usually at the grandparents' house. We prepare a big meal, eat a lot of traditional food, and catch up with each other. Kids get pocket money from their elders, which they love. Besides that, we celebrate birthdays, weddings, and a baby's first birthday. And in the workplace, we have company dinners with coworkers, which we call "hoesik". In general, food is at the center of everything. People eat, drink, talk, and laugh together for hours. That's how we show we care about each other.

The last one I went to was Chuseok, just a couple of weeks ago. My wife and I went to my father-in-law's house, since it's close to ours. The whole family was there, including my two brothers-in-law, my daughter Eunbin, and my son Suhyun. We arrived in the morning, and everyone was already busy in the kitchen. I helped out by carrying the dishes and setting the table. We had a huge meal: rice cakes, grilled fish, and lots of side dishes. After lunch, we sat around and chatted, and I played cards with my brothers-in-law and my son. Later in the afternoon, we went on a short walk to burn off some of the food. It was just a simple day, but I really enjoyed it. Spending time with family always recharges me.

One I'll never forget was my father-in-law's birthday party last year. My wife and her two brothers planned a surprise party, and I was in charge of keeping him away from the house. I took him out for a "quick coffee". We ended up talking for two hours! Meanwhile, my wife kept texting me: "Keep him there a little longer!" I was sweating the whole time. When we finally got home, everyone was hiding in the dark. The lights came on, and everyone shouted "Surprise!" But my father-in-law just stood there, completely confused. He thought we'd gotten the wrong house! Then he started laughing, and his eyes got a little teary. It was so touching. It was unforgettable because he's usually such a serious, quiet man, and that was the first time I saw him so emotional.

Hi, I'm looking for a desk for my home office. I saw a wooden one on your website, the "Oslo" model, and I'd like to ask a few questions. First, what are the dimensions? I need it to fit in a small room.. Great. And what is it made of? Is it solid wood?. I see. How many colors does it come in? I'm thinking about walnut or white.. One last question: does the price include delivery and assembly? And how long does it take to arrive?. That sounds good. Thank you so much for your help!

Hello, I'm calling about a desk I bought from your store last week. I have a bit of a problem. When I put it together, I found a big scratch on the top, and one of the legs doesn't fit properly, so the desk wobbles. I'm really disappointed, because I was looking forward to using it. First, could you send someone to fix it at my house? If that's not possible, could you send me a brand-new desk? Or, if you don't have any in stock, I'd be happy to get a refund. Any of those would work for me. I'd really appreciate your help. Thank you!

Yes, and it involved my biggest passion: coffee. A few years ago, I splurged on an expensive espresso machine. I was so excited. The first morning, I made a cup, and I felt like a real barista. But the next day, water started leaking all over the kitchen counter! I thought maybe I'd done something wrong, so I read the manual and tried again. Same thing. It was clearly a defect. I called customer service, and they were kind of slow at first. But I sent them a video of the leak, and they agreed to send a replacement. A few days later, the new machine arrived, and it worked perfectly. Since then, I always check reviews and keep the receipt. And of course, I never go a day without my espresso!

I'd like to compare my wife and my daughter, Eunbin. They're actually quite similar in some ways. They're both really kind, and they both love trying new food. They also have a good sense of humor, so I laugh a lot around both of them. But they're very different in other ways. My wife is outgoing and spontaneous. She'll say, "Let's just go!" and figure it out later. She makes friends wherever she goes. Eunbin, on the other hand, is shy and quiet, and she's a planner. When we go on a trip, she makes a detailed schedule for everything. In that way, she's more like me. I think I need both of them in my life. One keeps me adventurous, and the other keeps me organized.

With my wife, we talk about pretty much everything: work, dinner plans, and where to go on the weekend. With my friends, it's mostly games, work stress, and old memories. We laugh about stupid things from the old days. The last conversation I had was with my wife, last night, actually. We were sitting on the couch with a cup of coffee, and we talked about where to go to see the fall foliage. She wanted to go to a famous mountain, but I said it'd be too crowded. We went back and forth for a while, and in the end, we decided to leave early to beat the crowds. It wasn't a serious talk, but I love moments like that. Those little conversations are what keep us close.
